correctness.rationale: Trace and off-diagonal frame identities reduce exactly to Fourier moments on D=A-A. A putative support of at most |D|-1 leads to a nonsingular prime Fourier subminor forcing all weights zero, while Caratheodory compresses the uniform p-node Parseval rule to at most |D| positive nodes. Chebotarev also guarantees unique weights and an affine-independent simplex criterion. Cauchy-Davenport and Vosper, with the unsaturated bound 2k-1<=p-2, give the sharp fixed-cardinality optimum and progressions; cyclotomic irreducibility forces p equal-weight nodes when |A|>=2. The p=2 and singleton cases and composite counterexample were checked. Supplementary finite tests: 436 configurations, not an infinite certificate.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2026 finite Gabor frame paper has different block-operator hypotheses and does not state this all-support positive-frame cardinality law. The closest published positive three-site theorem is a single spatial configuration; its prime case is implied by the present universal result, while the opposite implication is absent. A published unweighted prime-power sampling theorem has an equal-weight assumption and cannot cover the strictly smaller positive-weight designs here. The exact all-support |A-A| budget, simplex characterization and Vosper equality classification were not found in the consulted full texts/semantic searches. Classical minor, convex and sumset ingredients are acknowledged; latent equivalent cubature literature remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: The all-support statement is a concise synthesis of classical Chebotarev and Caratheodory theorems, and may occur without the same terminology in positive quadrature or scalable harmonic frame literature.

value.rationale: The exact minimum acquisition budget for arbitrary prime-order spatial apertures is the natural and computable difference-set cardinality |A-A|, not an arbitrary finite example. The theorem supplies a complete exact test and uniqueness for optimal frequency weights, classifies minimal-budget spatial sets via additive structure, and yields arbitrarily large savings over equal-weight sampling. These results address natural Fourier frame design and known motivating unsolved longer-aperture cases even though the proof uses established theorems.
